# Mini App Factory

> A Cloudflare-first application factory. Describe an app in plain language, read
> the files it produces, and publish them into your own Cloudflare account.

## Overview

Mini App Factory turns a natural-language description into a real project of
ordinary web files, previews it, and deploys it to Cloudflare. Output is
portable: standard web files and standard Wrangler configuration, exportable as
a zip or a GitHub repo.

## Build targets

Every project is one of two shapes, derived from its files rather than set as a
mode.

- **Static site** — HTML, CSS, browser JS. Uploaded to Cloudflare Pages as an
  asset bundle. Nothing billable is created.
- **Edge app** — the same bundle plus `_worker.js` and, usually, stored data
  through D1, KV, R2, Queues, Vectorize, or Durable Objects, declared in
  `cloudflare.manifest.json`.

## Key Features

- **Two targets, one host** — static sites and full edge apps from the same
  description, both deployed to Cloudflare
- **Confirmed provisioning** — the exact list of Cloudflare resources, labelled
  create or reuse, is approved before anything is created
- **Guarded migrations** — an applied migration cannot be edited afterwards and
  destructive ones are refused
- **Live preview** — files render in memory as you type; an edge app can also
  run against a throwaway Cloudflare preview deployment
- **Element selector** — click an element in the preview to jump to its line or
  attach it to the next request
- **Build and Discuss modes** — Build writes files, Discuss never does
- **Restorable versions** — every successful build is kept
- **Export** — a zip with a generated README, or a push to a repo you own
- **Live model list** — fetched from the providers on every visit, never
  hardcoded; bring your own key per provider

## Pages

- `/` — landing page and the composer
- `/dashboard` — projects, filterable by deploy state and build target
- `/edit/[projectName]` — the workspace: conversation, files, preview, code
- `/edit/[projectName]/settings` — deployment, Cloudflare, access, architecture,
  project memory, metadata
- `/settings` — connected accounts and API keys
- `/admin`, `/admin/models` — provider and model administration
- `/docs` — documentation
- `/support`, `/privacy`, `/eula`

## Tech Stack

- Next.js 16 (App Router)
- Convex (database and server functions)
- Stack Auth
- Cloudflare Pages, Workers, D1, KV, R2, Queues
- TypeScript, Tailwind CSS v4
- The Plate design system: `app/globals.css` and `components/kit/`
